title: 3 Stocks to Buy Before Midterms (Get PAID No Matter Who Wins)
creator: MarketBeat
summary: MarketBeat interviews Mark Lichtenfeld (The Oxford Club) in Savannah on getting paid whatever the midterm outcome: do not invest on polls, stay the course if long-term, and own dividend payers across three sectors. Financials: Lincoln National (LNC) — BUY, insurers gain as rates rise, annuity demand, de-risked via reinsurance, 4.5% yield. Healthcare: AbbVie (ABBV) — BUY, long-time favourite, perpetual dividend raiser, Q2 revenue +10%, ~18x earnings. Energy: Phillips 66 (PSX) — BUY, his favourite refiner; Hormuz risk premium keeps oil elevated and Wall Street's expected 2027 earnings decline looks too pessimistic. All three are first tracked MarketBeat calls; no flips, no share prices stated.

calls.video_title: 3 Stocks to Buy Before Midterms (Get PAID No Matter Who Wins)
calls.thesis: Guest Mark Lichtenfeld: first tracked MarketBeat call on Lincoln National, presented as a stock to buy before the midterms. Insurers thrive as rates rise gradually — they earn more on invested premiums while payouts stay fixed; Lincoln is a big seller of popular fixed annuities, has de-risked liabilities via reinsurance, and pays a 4.5% dividend yield. He says financials have pulled back and this is a good time to be buying them.

calls.video_title: 3 Stocks to Buy Before Midterms (Get PAID No Matter Who Wins)
calls.thesis: Guest Mark Lichtenfeld: first tracked MarketBeat call on AbbVie, a long-time favourite presented as a buy. Biopharma giant, perpetual dividend raiser (raised every year since the Abbott spin-off), huge drug pipeline and portfolio including leading cancer drugs, strong acquisition history; Q2 revenue up 10%. At ~18x earnings it is not dirt cheap, but steady growth should continue and all-time highs do not deter him.

calls.video_title: 3 Stocks to Buy Before Midterms (Get PAID No Matter Who Wins)
calls.thesis: Guest Mark Lichtenfeld: first tracked MarketBeat call on Phillips 66, his favourite refiner, recommended before the war started. Refiner margins have surged, a lasting Strait of Hormuz risk premium should keep oil well above $40-50, and the dividend has been raised for over a decade. Wall Street expects ~7% earnings decline next year after this year's surge; he thinks that is too pessimistic and positive growth would be a major catalyst.
